While this protein is normally helpful, playing a role in DNA repair and stabilization, the way it works can inadvertently worsen the genetic “repeats” associated with some neurodegenerative disorders. In Huntington’s, for example, a three-letter DNA sequence repeats an unusually large number of times. Those extra copies lead the cell to produce an abnormal version of the “huntingtin” protein, which then damages the nerves. LoQus23’s drug — codenamed LQT-23 — isn’t yet in human testing. But the company said it expects to “in the near future” submit an application to begin a clinical trial. The LoQus23 team “has been motivated by the ambition to create a disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s disease,” said Reynolds, who serves as the company’s CEO, in a statement. “This transaction brings that ambition one step closer, as Lilly has the neuroscience track record, scale, and expertise to accelerate LQT-23 into and through the clinic.” Flush with cash from its popular obesity medications, Lilly has inked more than a dozen acquisitions this year. Just last week, the pharmaceutical giant announced its purchase of blood cancer specialist Calytrix Bio in a deal that could be worth up to $1.5 billion. At least four of Lilly’s buyouts have carried upfront payments of $50 million or more, according to data compiled by BioPharma Dive. Two of those larger transactions focused on neuroscience. Lilly paid $6.3 billion for Centessa Pharmaceuticals, a major bet on an emerging class of sleep medicines that Wall Street analysts believe will drive billions of dollars in sales. Lilly also broke into the burgeoning psychedelics space by buying AtaiBeckley through a deal valued at $2.8 billion. content: An article from Dive Brief Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal For $550 million up front, Argenx will take control of Unnatural Products’ “macrocyclic peptide” technology and direct it to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a maker of "macrocyclic peptides," on Nov. 9, 2026. deliormanli via Getty Images Dive Brief: Argenx, a Netherlands-based biotechnology company focused on antibody drugs, on Monday said it has agreed to acquire a protein specialist in a potentially billion-dollar-plus deal. Unnatural Products has a platform that pairs machine learning, screening and other techniques to engineer “macrocyclic peptides.” These peptides are larger and more complex than typical small molecules, which allows them to more effectively bind to tricky proteins and address some challenging diseases. Yet, they’re still tiny enough that they can be swallowed. Argenx plans to use the platform to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. The acquisition carries a $550 million upfront cash payment. Unnatural Products could receive up to $595 million more if specific milestones are hit. In 2020, for example, Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ Imcivree was cleared as a treatment for certain genetic forms of obesity. The following year, Aurinia Pharmaceuticals’ Lupkynis became the first-ever oral medicine for adults with active lupus nephritis. In 2023, the FDA greenlit a UCB medicine called Zilbrysq for “generalized myasthenia gravis,” a rare autoimmune condition that’s become somewhat of a battleground for several developers. Argenx’s own flagship product, Vyvgart, targets this disease and brought in $4.5 billion in net product sales from January through the end of September. Thomas Smith, a Leerink Partners analyst who covers Argenx, wrote in a note to clients that the new acquisition “represents potential for longer-term strategic value.” He explained there’s a desire — both in big pharma and in the broader immunology and inflammation research space — to make oral, long-acting therapeutics that are able to be more effective and convenient than conventional biologics. The Unnatural Products deal, which comes on the heels of Argenx’s potentially $2.2 billion purchase of Forte Biosciences, also “signals further focus on pipeline growth and diversification,” Smith wrote. content: An article from Dive Brief Pfizer leaps into ‘in vivo’ CAR-T with latest China deal The potentially $2.6 billion collaboration puts Pfizer into a competitive race to treat autoimmune conditions by reprogramming cells inside the body. Published Nov. 18, 2026 By Kristin Jensen Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Pfizer will work with Starna Therapeutics to develop "in vivo" cell therapies for autoimmune disease. Jeenah Moon via Getty Images Dive Brief: Pfizer is undertaking yet another deal in China to get into a budding area of research, using “in vivo” cell therapy for autoimmune diseases. Under the terms of the agreement with Starna Therapeutics, Pfizer will obtain exclusive rights outside Greater China to three preclinical programs focused on autoimmune diseases. It will also get the rights to use Starna’s technology in inflammation, immunology and oncology as well as options to license other projects and expand its territory to include Greater China. Pfizer will pay Starna $330 million up front and offer as much as $2.3 billion more in payments for reaching certain development and commercial milestones. Though this would be its first venture into this particular area of research, the company on Wednesday emphasized its experience with RNA-based medicines after the success of the COVID-19 vaccine Comirnaty. Pfizer said it would manufacture the products for clinical trials in the U.S. Starna is developing RNA medicines that are designed to reprogram cells inside the body — or “in vivo” — while also branching into fields beyond oncology. Marketed CAR-T cell cancer therapies such as Johnson & Johnson’s Carvykti use an “ex vivo” process that involves harvesting a patient’s cells, modifying them and infusing them back into the body. Drugmakers like Starna are hoping that they can eliminate much of the complicated and lengthy process involved in making an ex vivo CAR-T therapy as well as avoid the chemotherapy “conditioning” that typically accompanies it. The in vivo work is still in early stages, but it’s drawn a lot of attention. Just in the last two years, AstraZeneca, AbbVie, Gilead Sciences and Bristol Myers Squibb have all undertaken acquisitions centered on the technology. Eli Lilly, meanwhile, has announced two buyouts this year alone. Many drugmakers are now pursuing a similar strategy to Pfizer and Starna’s, hoping that the therapies can treat conditions such as lupus and multiple sclerosis in addition to cancer. Research released a few years ago suggested that CAR-T treatments can “reset” the immune system, and ex vivo therapies are getting closer to market for that use. But there are also questions; Novartis and Bristol Myers both recently paused trials of CAR-T therapies in autoimmune conditions because of safety concerns. For Pfizer, the Starna deal marks at least the fifth major alliance with a Chinese company since the start of 2025, and the company is far from alone in pursuing drug candidates in the country. The trend has become so pronounced that the industry trade group BIO recently unveiled a five-year plan to help prop up the U.S. biotechnology industry in the face of Chinese competition. content: An article from News roundup FDA publishes rejection letter for Summit drug; Nuvalent buyout pays more dividends for GSK The FDA had several issues with ivonescimab, according to the letter. Elsewhere, Sellas shares rocketed on results for a leukemia vaccine and Biogen and Lilly struck up new R&D pacts. Published Nov. 18, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving Summit Therapeutics and Sellas Life Sciences, as well as updates from GSK, AstraZeneca, Eli Lilly and Biogen that you may have missed. The Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday released a complete response letter detailing why it rejected Summit Therapeutics and Akeso’s ivonescimab for lung cancer. Summit said Sunday that the FDA’s decision was driven by the lack of clear survival benefit. The agency, though, also expressed concerns with the magnitude of the drug’s impact on tumor progression and how relevant the findings were to U.S. patients, according to the letter. Ivonescimab’s “modest” benefits don’t outweigh its additive safety risks, the regulator said, adding that Summit should run a new trial to win a clearance. In a statement Friday, Capricor revealed that the agency had issued a rejection letter for deramiocel, a cellular medicine it’s been developing for the progressive neuromuscular disorder. Those issues — which included violations of study blinding protocols and after-the-fact changes to the statistical analysis plan — compromised Capricor’s findings, the FDA said. “This was not a decision made lightly. Upholding rigorous evidentiary standards is precisely how the FDA protects patients, particularly those living with rare diseases, from interventions whose benefits have not been sufficiently established,” the regulator added. “We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval,” countered CEO Linda Marbán, in Capricor’s statement. “We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.” Deramiocel is made from donor-derived heart cells able to preserve certain cardiac and muscle function. Capricor had initially developed the therapy for a fatal, heart-related complication of Duchenne, and early testing showed deramiocel's potential to help the heart pump blood. Capricor aimed for an approval based on results from a small trial and data from a historical study of heart function. Yet in July 2025, FDA officials rejected deramiocel, saying the company hadn't proven the therapy’s effectiveness and needed additional data. Capricor claimed to have been blindsided by the ruling. “We are surprised by this decision by the FDA,” Marbán said in a statement at the time. Marbán added that the company had followed the agency's guidance and that the review had previously advanced with “no major issues.” if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Capricor soon after announced that the FDA would reconsider the rejection based on new data from a late-stage study of deramiocel called “HOPE-3.” Last December, it revealed the treatment hit both of its main objectives in that study, helping preserve upper limb as well as heart function. Those claims were intensely debated when the FDA convened a panel of experts to review Capricor's application in July. In briefing documents ahead of the meeting, FDA scientists argued deramiocel had actually failed the trial and tinkered with statistical analyses to produce a more compelling story. Capricor countered and said that agency staff relied on an outdated analysis. The same day, HOPE-3 study results were published in The Lancet and conflicted with claims Capricor had previously made, forcing the company to issue a clarification in a regulatory filing. The advisory committee ultimately sided with the FDA's assessment, with a majority of panelists concluding testing hadn't shown clear evidence of deramiocel's effectiveness. Panelists instead expressed more support for its potential impact on upper limb function. The FDA, which originally sought to respond to Capricor by late August, extended its review of deramiocel to Nov. 22 after Capricor said it would instead seek clearance in a “refined” indication “focused on upper limb function.” More than two dozen trial investigators and physicians also penned a letter of support for approval to regulators in recent weeks. Deramiocel’s review is “clearly a case where regulatory flexibility can be applied,” that group wrote. Rejection “would signal complete inflexibility on the part of the agency, contradicting the core values articulated” by its stance on rare disease drug reviews. Under previous FDA leadership, a handful of drugmakers claimed to have been stunned by a sudden shift in regulatory guidance. Yet since the resignations of ex-commissioner Marty Makary and top deputy Vinay Prasad, U.S. regulators have changed their stance on a number of these decisions. They've also taken steps to show the agency will be more flexible in evaluating rare disease treatments. “[The] FDA approaches rare disease applications with every intention of finding a path forward,” it said Friday, upon rejecting Capricor’s application. “[H]owever, flexibility in regulatory approach cannot come at the cost of the foundational requirement that the data underlying an approval decision be reliable.” Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: FDA, Gene Therapy

content: STAT PlusPharma FDA approves new breast cancer drug, providing new option for some patients, boost for Roche Company believes therapy could become its top-selling product, though estimates vary Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Xavier GALIANA/AFP via Getty Images By Andrew JosephNov. 16, 2026 Europe Correspondent Andrew Joseph[email protected]Andrew covers the biopharma industry, scientific research, and public health across the continent. You can reach Andrew confidentially on Signal at drewqjoseph.71. The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved a new breast cancer drug from Roche, teeing up the launch of a medicine that the Swiss company has said could become its top-selling product ever. The approval of Wilserdly, also known as giredestrant, was one of the most important regulatory decisions Roche had been awaiting. It also gives the company another foothold in breast cancer treatments, a field in which it has a storied history with the drug Herceptin through its subsidiary Genentech, though in recent years it’s fallen behind rival pharma companies in oncology. Advertisement The approval is specifically for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that has picked up a mutation in the ESR1 gene, a sign that the tumor is developing resistance to standard treatments. The evERA trial showed that the drug, an oral treatment known as a selective estrogen receptor degrader, or SERD, extended the time period before patients’ tumors progressed. The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved Bayer’s drug to reduce recurrence of stroke, making available the first in a novel class of medications that hold the promise of preventing blood clots more safely. Many blood thinners aren’t used in this setting due to the increased risk of bleeding. But Bayer’s drug, which will be sold under the brand name Sunharbo, inhibits a protein called XIa, utilizing a mechanism that’s thought to stop the formation of bad clots without increasing the risk of bleeding.Advertisement Related Story Lowering blood pressure after stroke or with diabetes poses challenges, in research and practice In a Phase 3 trial that enrolled people who had already had a stroke and were taking common stroke treatments, 8.4% of participants who took placebo experienced a secondary stroke, while 6.2% of patients who took Sunharbo experienced one, translating into a 26% risk reduction. Another way to look at the data is that in one year, 53 patients need to be treated for one recurrent stroke to be prevented. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? content: STAT PlusOpinionAdam’s Take FDA rejects Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne therapy, a decision that was a long time coming A public pressure campaign couldn’t alter the hard reality: The drug didn’t work Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Sarah Silbiger/Getty Images By Adam FeuersteinNov. 20, 2026 Adam Feuerstein, a senior writer and biotech columnist, is the author of Adam’s Biotech Scorecard, a subscriber-only newsletter about the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. He is also a co-host of the weekly biotech podcast The Readout Loud and author of the newsletter Adam’s Biotech Scorecard. You can reach Adam on Signal at stataf.54. The Food and Drug Administration said Friday that it had rejected a cell therapy intended for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy developed by Capricor Therapeutics. The decision to block the treatment, called deramiocel, from reaching the market should have been an easy one for regulators to make. The targeted patient population — teenagers and young men with Duchenne who had already lost the ability to walk — have few treatment options today. Deramiocel didn’t help them either. Capricor conducted two randomized clinical trials. Both failed to show deramiocel could stave off heart failure or preserve muscle function in their arms. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 国产首个！翰森制药氘索昔替尼上市申请获受理，1类新药TYK2变构抑制剂直指成人中重度斑块状银屑病 国产首个！翰森制药氘索昔替尼上市申请获受理，1类新药TYK2变构抑制剂直指成人中重度斑块状银屑病 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 11:51 1258 TYK2 翰森制药集团有限公司 银屑病 HS-10374 片 CMS-D001片 11月20日，CDE官网显示，翰森制药自主研发的1类新药 氘索昔替尼（HS-10374）上市申请获受理，拟用于治疗成人中重度斑块状银屑病。这也是国产首个申报上市的TYK2变构抑制剂。图源：CDE官网HS-10374是一款口服高选择性TYK2变构抑制剂，可抑制白细胞介素-12（IL-12）、IL-23及I型干扰素（IFN）通路的信号传导，在多种自身免疫性疾病领域具有潜在治疗价值。一、Ⅲ期临床达到主要终点，近1/3患者实现PASI 100今年9月，翰森制药宣布，HS-10374治疗成人中重度斑块状银屑病的Ⅲ期临床研究达到共同主要终点及多项次要终点。研究结果显示，治疗第16周，HS-10374组达到银屑病面积和严重程度指数较基线改善至少75%（PASI 75）的患者比例，以及达到静态医师整体评估评分0或1、且较基线至少改善2分（sPGA 0/1）的患者比例，均显著高于安慰剂组。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库更值得关注的是，在第16周，HS-10374组超过半数患者达到PASI 90应答，近1/3患者达到PASI 100应答，展现出较好的皮损改善效果。安全性方面，HS-10374表现出良好的安全性和耐受性，其安全性特征与同类TYK2抑制剂类似，未观察到新的安全性信号。二、国产TYK2赛道升温，多款新药进入后期临床TYK2是JAK激酶家族的重要成员，参与IL-12、IL-23及I型干扰素等多种细胞因子的信号传导。通过选择性抑制TYK2相关信号通路，有望在调节异常免疫反应的同时，为银屑病等自身免疫性疾病提供新的口服治疗选择。从全球研发格局来看，目前已获批上市的选择性TYK2抑制剂仅有一款，即百时美施贵宝（BMS）的氘可来昔替尼（Deucravacitinib）。此外，武田的zasocitinib已于今年9月在美国申报上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库国内企业也在加快TYK2抑制剂的研发推进。除翰森制药的HS-10374外，益方生物的nomelcitinib（D-2570）已完成Ⅲ期临床研究，尚未递交上市申请；北京诺诚健华的fadeucravacitinib也已顺利完成Ⅲ期临床研究；海思科的envudeucitinib（ESK-001）已授权Alumis，Ⅲ期临床研究取得积极进展。此外，据摩熵医药数据库显示，国内还有多款TYK2抑制剂进入Ⅱ期临床阶段，包括康哲药业的CMS-D001、微芯生物的CS-32582、祐森健恒的UA-021、上海致根医药的ZG-002及安锐生物的ARTS-011等。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库三、结语随着HS-10374率先递交上市申请，国产TYK2变构抑制剂开始向商业化阶段迈进。未来，随着更多候选药物陆续完成临床开发并推进上市，TYK2抑制剂在银屑病等自身免疫性疾病领域的竞争有望进一步加剧。 The Food and Drug Administration rejected a treatment for a type of lung cancer developed by the U.S.-based biotech Summit Therapeutics and the Chinese drugmaker Akeso, Summit said on Sunday. In a letter sent to the companies, FDA regulators said the drug, called ivonescimab, could not be approved because it didn’t help patients live longer. While the drug was found to slow lung cancer worsening in patients, the absence of a survival benefit “does not support the positive benefit-risk profile in support of approval,” FDA reviewers concluded. content: An article from Dive Brief Kymera eczema pill meets goals in mid-stage trial The protein degrader drug showed “biologic-like efficacy,” according to Wall Street analysts who argued it could challenge Sanofi and Regeneron’s market leader Dupixent. Published Nov. 23, 2026 Jonathan Gardner Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Dive Brief: A protein degrading eczema drug developed by Kymera Therapeutics met the main goals of a Phase 2 clinical trial, significantly reducing disease severity in enrollees who got it compared with those given a placebo, the company said Monday. Codenamed KT-621, the drug demonstrated efficacy comparable to injectable biologics like Sanofi and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals’ Dupixent, according to Wall Street analysts. One of the tested doses achieved an average 72% reduction on an eczema severity scale after 16 weeks, 45 percentage points greater than in enrollees who got a placebo. Kymera said it plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in eczema — also called atopic dermatitis — by mid-2027, while a Phase 2 trial in asthma is expected to read out by late next year. Dupixent is in its 10th year on the market and is due to lose patent-protected exclusivity in the U.S. in 2032. KT-621, therefore, must compete not just with Dupixent and other biologics like Eli Lilly’s Ebglyss, but also any biosimilars that can be expected to soon enter the market after key patents expire. With KT-621, Kymera is seeking to tamp down the same inflammatory processes as Dupixent and Ebglyss. But instead of blocking signaling proteins related to allergic conditions, it degrades a transcription factor on the same pathway by triggering cellular trash disposal systems. The trial Kymera reported today, titled BROADEN2, enrolled 244 people and randomized them into four roughly equal-sized groups to take one of three doses of KT-621 or a placebo. The primary goal was the score on a scale called the Eczema Area and Severity Index, or EASI. The best score of 72% reduction came from the people who got the mid-dose, with the low-dose group seeing their EASI scores drop 64% and the high dose 61%. As a secondary goal, the trial also measured the proportion of patients who had a 75% reduction in their EASI scores. In the mid-dose group, 62% achieved this mark, compared with 22% of the placebo group. The drug also appeared safe, with most side effects proving mild or moderate. Higher rates of conjunctivitis, a known side effect, were detected in the people receiving the study drug, but none of the people who got it quit taking the drug. Four other serious adverse events were reported, though none were judged to be related to the drug. Wall Street analysts said the data show KT-621 has “biologic-like efficacy,” putting it in a position to challenge Dupixent and related medicines. “Overall, we believe the balance of topline data is strongly supportive of an effective oral treatment option with clean safety/tolerability — a uniquely competitive profile across the [eczema] field, capable of both taking share and expanding the addressable market,” wrote Leerink Research analyst Thomas Smith in a client note. content: STAT PlusBiotech Kymera Therapeutics reports mid-stage eczema trial success for would-be Dupixent rival Study was seen as one of this year’s most impactful immunology drug readouts Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Eczema is defined by patches of itchy, dry, and bumpy skin that flare due to immune inflammation.Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 23, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. In a closely watched trial seen as one of this year’s most impactful immunology drug readouts, Kymera Therapeutics announced on Monday that its experimental therapy effectively and safely treated eczema patients’ itchy, inflamed skin. In the Phase 2 trial, moderate-to-severe eczema patients randomly assigned to receive the biotech’s pill, KT-621, showed a statistically significant reduction in disease severity compared with those given a placebo. This was true across all three doses tested after 16 weeks of treatment, with a peak placebo-adjusted improvement of 45% among those given a moderate dose. Patients on this dose were also more likely to see an improvement of 75% or more in disease severity, with 62% of treated participants clearing that bar compared with 22% of the placebo group.Advertisement The BROADEN2 trial succeeded across all primary and secondary endpoints, including itch reduction and the fraction of patients who achieved clear or almost-clear skin. KT-621 was also generally safe and well tolerated. The only side effect that was more common among patients on the drug was conjunctivitis (i.e. pink eye), which appeared in 20%, 13%, and 11% of patients on a low, middle, and high dose, respectively. All of these cases were mild to moderate, and none caused participants to stop treatment. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? mm²。其中，2例患者既往接受过T细胞特异性双抗治疗。在这样的患者人群中，KJ-C2529取得了3例CR、2例PR的初步疗效。尤其是起始剂量1.2×10⁸ TU即观察到CR，最长缓解持续时间已接近5个月，且所有缓解在数据截止时仍在持续。随着后续剂量探索和随访时间延长，其疗效表现仍有待进一步观察。双抗经治患者的表现也提供了值得关注的线索：2例患者中，1例获得CR；另一例则因T细胞耗竭及CD20抗原丢失，未观察到有效的CAR-T扩增。这一差异提示，体内CAR-T的治疗效果不仅与载体递送效率有关，也可能受到患者自身T细胞功能状态及肿瘤靶抗原表达的影响。二、0例IRR、0例DLT，完全B细胞清除拓展应用想象空间除了疗效，KJ-C2529的初步安全性表现同样值得关注。在6例患者中，未观察到治疗相关严重不良事件（SAE）、剂量限制性毒性（DLT）及输注相关反应（IRR），也未出现免疫效应细胞相关神经毒性综合征（ICANS）、免疫效应细胞相关噬血细胞性淋巴组织细胞增多症样综合征（IEC-HS）及与输注相关的细胞因子双相增高，仅出现1级细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）。血液学毒性总体较轻。除1例无法完全排除与疾病相关的3级白细胞减少外，未发生其他与治疗相关的3级及以上血液学毒性。其中，未观察到IRR及严重免疫相关毒性，为KJ-C2529后续探索更便捷的给药和治疗管理模式提供了积极信号。不过，目前样本量仅为6例，其安全性仍需更大规模临床研究验证。另一项值得关注的结果是，所有达到缓解的患者均观察到完全B细胞清除。这一现象也让KJ-C2529未来的应用探索不再局限于血液肿瘤。近年来，CAR-T在自身免疫性疾病领域的研究持续推进，深度清除异常B细胞是相关治疗策略的重要方向。KJ-C2529此次观察到的B细胞清除结果，为其未来向自身免疫性疾病等B细胞相关疾病拓展提供了初步依据，但具体疗效仍有待临床研究验证。下一步，KJ-C2529将进一步扩大剂量探索范围，明确潜在的推荐II期剂量（RP2D）及剂量－反应关系，预计于2027年上半年申报注册临床试验。从首次披露的人体数据来看，KJ-C2529已初步展现出体内CAR-T的临床应用潜力。随着后续研究推进，其疗效持续性、安全性及适应症拓展空间值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] content: STAT PlusPharma In a win for MAHA, FDA creates new regulatory category for the supplement NAC NAC has been sold as a dietary supplement for years Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Margaret MantoNov. 16, 2026 Washington Correspondent Margaret Manto[email protected]Margaret is a Washington correspondent covering the Food and Drug Administration and other federal health agencies. Reach her on Signal at margaretmanto.61. WASHINGTON — The Food and Drug Administration is proposing a new classification for a product that’s existed in a legal gray area for years, a win for proponents of dietary supplements, including members of the MAHA movement. The proposed rule would classify N-acetyl-L-cysteine, known as NAC and already widely sold over the counter, as the agency’s first “Dietary Ingredient Not Excluded from the Dietary Supplement Definition” — in essence, not not a supplement. Advertisement The need for the legal backbending stems from the fact that the FDA previously approved NAC as a drug, and FDA regulations prohibit the agency from including approved drugs in the dietary supplement category. In 1963, the agency approved NAC to break up mucus in certain lung conditions, and in 1985 to treat acetaminophen overdose. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved the first drug to treat limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, a broad collection of progressive muscle conditions that has long received scant attention from physicians and drug developers. The drug, developed by BridgeBio under the name ribitol and marketed as Welgemda, is specifically approved for patients with LGMD 2i/R9, a subtype the company estimates affects 2,000 to 3,000 patients in the U.S. and another 4,000 to 5,000 in Europe. Advertisement BridgeBio said Monday it will charge insurers $75,446.58 for a 28-day supply of medicine — meaning the price will be just a hair under $1 million per year. title: 全球首款CFB/MASP-2双抗获批临床！华东医药HDM4002双通路阻断，剑指IgA肾病肾功能损失
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 全球首款CFB/MASP-2双抗获批临床！华东医药HDM4002双通路阻断，剑指IgA肾病肾功能损失 全球首款CFB/MASP-2双抗获批临床！华东医药HDM4002双通路阻断，剑指IgA肾病肾功能损失 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 11:18 1421 CFB HER2 MASP2 华东医药股份有限公司 非小细胞肺癌 国产IgA肾病创新药研发再迎新进展！11月17日，CDE官网显示，华东医药旗下1类创新生物药HDM4002注射液获批临床，拟用于治疗具有疾病进展风险的原发性免疫球蛋白A（IgA）肾病成人患者，以减少肾功能损失。图源：华东医药企业公告与此同时，华东医药旗下多款产品及合作产品被纳入2026年新版国家医保药品目录及商业健康保险创新药品目录，研发与商业化两端均有新进展。一、全球首款CFB/MASP-2双抗，瞄准IgA肾病HDM4002由杭州中美华东制药有限公司研发并拥有全球知识产权，是一款1类生物新药。IgA肾病的发生发展与免疫异常及补体系统过度激活密切相关。其中，补体旁路途径（AP）和凝集素途径（LP）是重要的疾病相关通路，CFB和MASP-2分别参与这两条通路的激活，也是当前补体靶向治疗的重要研究靶点。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库目前，针对CFB或MASP-2的单靶点药物已在IgA肾病领域展开临床探索。与之不同，HDM4002采用单分子双靶点设计，可同时靶向CFB和MASP-2，干预补体旁路途径与凝集素途径，旨在从两条补体激活通路入手，实现双重阻断，为IgA肾病治疗提供新的研发思路。从企业研发管线来看，华东医药今年以来也有多款创新药取得进展。据摩熵医药数据库显示，截至目前，华东医药已有4款1类新药进入获批临床及以上研发阶段。其中，HDM4002注射液、注射用HDM-2024均为今年首次获批临床的1类新药，目前HDM-2024已进入晚期实体瘤Ⅰ期临床研究阶段。 华东医药股份有限公司全球新药研发阶段分布 可直接点击跳转到数据库免费查看最新数据详细信息 图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库在临床前研究方面，公司披露的结果显示，HDM4002具有良好的成药性、安全性和有效性。不过，这些结果仍需通过临床研究进一步验证。根据本次临床试验通知书，该药针对IgA肾病将开展随机、双盲、安慰剂对照的Ⅰ期临床研究，其人体安全性及后续疗效表现仍有待观察。作为全球首款获批临床的CFB/MASP-2双靶点药物，HDM4002能否凭借双通路干预策略，在IgA肾病治疗中展现差异化优势，值得持续关注。二、多款产品新增纳入医保及商保目录除了创新药研发持续推进，华东医药现有产品的医保准入也迎来新进展，多款产品及合作产品被纳入2026年版医保及商保目录。11月14日，国家医保局、人力资源社会保障部发布2026年版国家基本医疗保险、生育保险和工伤保险药品目录，以及商业健康保险创新药品目录。华东医药部分产品及合作产品实现首次纳入、医保续约或目录调整。具体来看：马来酸美凡厄替尼片：首次纳入国家医保目录，用于具有EGFR外显子21（L858R）置换突变的局部晚期或转移性非小细胞肺癌成人患者的一线治疗。脯氨酸加格列净片：完成医保续约，支付标准与支付范围不变。他克莫司颗粒：调整至国家医保常规目录管理，支付范围保持不变。泽沃基奥仑赛注射液：继续纳入新版商业健康保险创新药品目录。新版药品目录将于2027年1月1日起正式执行。从创新药研发到产品医保准入，华东医药在研发创新与商业化布局方面均有新进展。一方面，HDM4002作为同时靶向CFB和MASP-2的双靶点创新药，为IgA肾病补体靶向治疗提供了新的研发方向；另一方面，多款产品及合作产品进入新版医保和商保目录，也为相关产品后续市场推广创造了条件。作为全球首款获批临床的CFB/MASP-2双靶点药物，HDM4002后续能否通过临床研究验证其双通路阻断策略，并在IgA肾病治疗中展现差异化优势，值得持续关注。 2026年11月20日，因诺惟康IVB105注射液收到美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)的新药临床试验（IND）许可，可正式进入临床试验阶段。IVB105注射液是基于因诺惟康自主研发的新型AAV衣壳平台开发的一款光遗传学基因治疗药物，靶向视网膜双极细胞，递送并表达覆盖广谱波长的光敏蛋白，拟用于治疗晚期视网膜色素变性（RP）。IVB105注射液也是目前国内唯一一款靶向视网膜双极细胞的光遗传学疗法。该药物作用机制不依赖于特定致病基因，不受患者基因型限制，通过绕过已经退化的光感受器，为不同基因型的晚期RP患者提供潜在治疗选择。项目顺利并提前获得FDA的IND许可，标志着因诺惟康在光遗传学基因治疗领域取得重要进展。关于因诺惟康北京因诺惟康医药科技有限公司（InnoVec Biotherapeutics Inc.）是一家以载体创新为驱动的临床阶段基因治疗公司。公司致力于开发适用于人体的基因治疗递送工具，解决递送工具开发中从动物到人转化困难的问题，目标找到所有组织和器官的基因递送工具，使基因治疗能够广泛应用到罕见疾病和常见疾病当中。因诺惟康拥有高效的技术开发，管线研发，工艺优化和临床运营团队，建立了领先技术开发平台，覆盖眼科，神经和肌肉等多个疾病领域，多个创新产品已经进入IIT和IND阶段。 近日，先声药业宣布，旗下独家创新药先必新®舌下片（依达拉奉右莰醇舌下片）通过2026年国家医保谈判，首次纳入国家医保目录；与此同时，先必新®注射液顺利完成第三次医保续约。图源：先声药业企业公告这意味着，先必新系列实现注射液与舌下片双剂型医保覆盖。新版国家医保目录将于2027年1月1日起正式实施，先必新系列的市场覆盖范围有望进一步扩大。一、首次纳入医保，舌下片拓展给药选择先必新舌下片于2024年11月获批上市，是先声药业在原有注射剂基础上开发的剂型改良新药，由先声药业与宁丹新药合作研发，主要用于改善急性缺血性脑卒中导致的神经症状、日常生活活动能力和功能障碍。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库与传统注射剂相比，舌下片采用舌下给药方式，可通过舌下静脉丛吸收入血，避免胃肠道吸收及肝脏首过效应，具有给药便捷等特点，也为患者出院后的序贯治疗提供了新的选择。值得关注的是，先必新舌下片此前还获得美国FDA突破性疗法认定（BTD），是全球脑卒中治疗领域首个获得该认定的创新药。此次首次纳入国家医保目录，将进一步改善该产品的支付可及性，也为其后续临床推广创造有利条件。二、注射液第三次续约，先必新系列完善产品布局作为先声药业脑卒中领域的核心产品，先必新注射液于2020年7月获批上市，是一款1类创新药，也是2015年以来全球卒中领域获批的首个创新药。该药由依达拉奉和右莰醇两种活性成分组成，按照5:1的比例配伍，通过抗氧化、清除自由基及抑制炎症等多重机制发挥脑神经保护作用，主要用于急性缺血性脑卒中治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库上市后，先必新注射液迅速放量，据摩熵医药数据库显示，注射液在医院端销售额在上市第2年近15亿元，第三年突破25亿元，成为先声药业重要的商业化产品之一。2025年销售额超25亿元，同比增长达9.49%，2026年前三季度销售额超30亿元，同比增长达64.40%。 图源：摩熵医药-医疗机构销售放大(2015至今)从临床需求来看，急性缺血性脑卒中约占全部卒中病例的85%以上。溶栓、取栓等再灌注治疗是急性期救治的重要手段，但部分患者即使恢复脑部血流，仍可能遗留不同程度的神经功能障碍，脑保护治疗仍具有临床需求。此次先必新注射液完成第三次医保续约，与舌下片首次纳入医保形成协同：注射液继续覆盖院内治疗场景，舌下片则凭借不同的给药方式，为患者提供新的治疗选择。结语从注射液到舌下片，先必新系列逐步形成双剂型产品布局。随着新版医保目录于2027年正式实施，双剂型医保覆盖有望进一步拓展产品的临床应用范围，也为先声药业脑卒中业务带来新的增长空间。
